reason: The no-JS safety predicate in RP-nojs is structurally blind to the only standards-conformant way to express a row-spanning native submit, so it false-passes. The embedded test scopes its search to page.locator("tr").filter({hasText: aName}).locator("form") — forms nested inside a <tr>. A <form> cannot legally wrap a <tr> or a whole <table>: the HTML parser foster-parents it out of the table (the 'in table' insertion mode). A row-spanning native submit therefore must be expressed as a <form> placed elsewhere in the document with an in-row <input type=file> and/or <button type=submit> associated via the form="<id>" attribute. In that valid, natural layout rawRows.locator("form") returns zero elements, the fill/click loops run zero times, attempted stays 0, and the sole browser-side assertion assert.deepEqual(posts, []) passes trivially. attempted is recorded in the step log but never asserted, and the Python-side _browser_case adds only assert after == before for RP-nojs, which is also trivially satisfied because the script never submits anything. Confirmed the current /sources page renders a real <table>/<tr> (ResponsiveTable) with only Link anchors and no native <form>, so the property is asserted against a DOM shape the parser itself cannot produce for row-spanning forms. Conclusion: the exact supplied test does NOT reject a real external-associated native submitter; it would pass while a no-JS user could click the in-row control and fire a mutation POST with no preflight. This is a genuine gap independent of the separate R4 repair, and it cannot be closed by requiring attempted > 0, because absence of native mutation controls is explicitly allowed by the outcome ('a safe form or file selector is not itself prohibited').
trivial_pass: Candidate renders a per-row native upload control as an external form plus form= association (valid HTML; the row stays a real <tr> so rawCount still equals 1): <form id="up-a" action="/upload/configured-csv" method="POST" enctype="multipart/form-data"><input type="hidden" name="source_asset_id" value="bank_partner_transactions"><input type="file" name="file"></form> placed as a sibling before the <table>, and inside the Bank Partner Transactions row <td>: <input type="file" form="up-a"> and <button type="submit" form="up-a">Upload to Bank Partner Transactions</button>. The RP-nojs script does: rawRows = page.locator("tr").filter({hasText:"Bank Partner Transactions"}) -> count 1 (passes rawCount==1); rawRows.locator("form") -> [] because no <form> is nested inside the <tr>; so the form/file/field/submit loops never execute, attempted stays 0, no POST is ever issued, posts stays [], and assert.deepEqual(posts,[]) passes, while the Python-side assert after==before also passes. A real no-JS user clicking the in-row button natively submits the external form to /upload/configured-csv (a mutation POST matching the /^\/upload\// && !/dry-run$/ changes filter) with no preflight dry-run gate. The same bypass works if the author wraps the whole <table> in a <form> — the parser foster-parents the form out, the row still matches, and rawRows.locator("form") is again empty.
